title: Moods, One Axis, Marker Pens & Thought Orbs
description: A blob avatar that is one path and a parameter table, single-axis scrollers, the highlight pseudos, reserved-space click states, and six dotted orbs.

drops.title: One Shape, Ten Moods
drops.description: A single closed SVG path springs between ten states — each mood is four harmonic amplitudes, a scale and a spin.
drops.concept: bloub rebuilt the x.ai bot avatar as one shape moving through fourteen states rather than a sprite sheet of poses. This reimplementation makes the parameter table the whole animation: the radius at each of 140 sampled angles is R·(1 + Σ aₖ·cos(kθ + φₖ)) for k = 2…5, so a 'mood' is just a seven-number vector that springs into place. Four avatars receive the same target on a stagger, so a state change travels down the row instead of four clones flipping together.
drops.source: jeremy-prt/bloub — SVG recreation of the x.ai bot avatar, one shape through 14 states

interaction.mouse: Tune stiffness, damping and wobble in the spring panel and watch the morph change character
interaction.click: Pick any of ten moods to retarget every avatar; picking one manually stops the auto-cycle
interaction.touch: Chips and sliders are full-size touch targets; the panel drops inline on narrow screens

drops.title: Carousels That Scroll One Way
drops.description: Chrome 153 lets overflow pair a scrollable value with clip, so a horizontal carousel stops being a vertical scroller too.
drops.concept: overflow-y: hidden never removed the scrollport — it only hid the bar, leaving a box whose scroll offset focus and anchoring can still move. Chrome 153 drops the old coercion so overflow: auto clip really does clip the cross axis. Two identical tracks sit side by side with a live probe of each one's vertical scroll range, plus a two-axis grid toggling scroll-axis-lock. Feature detection has to be behavioural: the shorthand has parsed for years, so the demo checks whether clip survives into the computed style.
drops.source: New in Chrome 153 — single-axis scroll containers

interaction.mouse: Scroll each track sideways, then push both down with scrollTop and watch which one moves
interaction.click: Set scrollTop = 40, focus the last off-screen card, or flip the axis lock on the 2-D grid
interaction.touch: Swipe the tracks; drag diagonally on the third to feel the axis lock engage

drops.title: The Browser's Marker Pens
drops.description: ::search-text, ::spelling-error, ::grammar-error and ::highlight() — four ways to repaint live text without moving a glyph.
drops.concept: Highlight pseudo-elements hand you the decorations the engine has always drawn for itself, with a deliberately tiny property set — colour, background-colour, text-decoration, text-shadow — because a highlight repaints and must never reflow. A live find bar drives the Custom Highlight API with the same recipe applied to ::search-text, so the treatment is visible even where find-in-page styling has not shipped; four switchable treatments stay inside what the spec allows.
drops.source: CSS-Tricks — styling ::search-text and other highlight-y pseudo-elements

interaction.mouse: Select text to see the restyled ::selection; press Ctrl/⌘+F to compare the browser's own find highlight
interaction.click: Switch between solid block, marker pen, wavy ink and glow treatments; step through matches
interaction.touch: Type in the find bar and tap the arrows; the editable paragraph shows live spelling and grammar squiggles

drops.title: The Half-Second After the Click
drops.description: Reserve every state's space before it arrives: a button that never resizes, a row that lands without a lurch, a drag you can abandon.
drops.concept: interior is a library built entirely around the moment after an interaction, where most interface jank actually lives. Three demonstrations isolate its rule: a save button measured against its widest future label so idle, pending and done all occupy one width — with a naive twin beside it for contrast; an optimistic list row that books its final height before springing in, and rolls back cleanly when the request fails; and a drag that treats pointercancel, window blur and tab-hide as designed exits that spring back to the committed value rather than freezing mid-gesture.
drops.source: ddoemonn/interior — micro-interactions for the half-second after a click

interaction.mouse: Run both buttons at once and watch the naive one resize while the reserved one holds; drag the slider
interaction.click: Add an optimistic row, add one that fails and rolls back, or simulate losing focus mid-drag
interaction.touch: Every control is tap-sized; the drag honours pointercancel, which is what a scroll steal looks like on a phone

drops.title: Six Orbs That Say What They're Doing
drops.description: Dotted thought orbs for agent UIs — searching is not solving, and listening is not weaving.
drops.concept: thinking-orbs replaces the one-size-fits-all spinner with a set of states an agent can actually be in, each a different way of placing dots on a plain 2-D canvas — no WebGL, no CSS filters, so it renders identically everywhere. Six states are rebuilt here: tilted orbits, a meridian sweeping a dotted globe, a waveform rolling through rings, a constellation wiring itself, a breathing ring, and a dotted outline stepping circle → triangle → square. Avatar and inline sizes are separate designs rather than one scaled, and the loop pauses itself off-screen.
drops.source: Jakubantalik/thinking-orbs — dotted thought-orb indicators for AI and agent UIs

interaction.mouse: Tune speed, dot size and density; flip to the light theme to see the palette follow
interaction.click: Pick any orb to drive the 64px chat avatar and the 20px inline indicator
interaction.touch: Tap a card to select it; the reduced-motion switch freezes every orb on a single frame
